overview:
ARCHITECTURE FOR SIX PARALLEL CUSTOMIZATION FEATURES (C1–C6). Read-only study of /Users/oleyyu/claude-ui-lab; nothing was edited.

Facts the design is built on:
1. Preferences live in <userData>/preferences.json. They are written only through desktop:call "settings" (main.cjs ~L872), which runs settingsPatch() from app/electron/preferences.mjs plus desktopPatch(). Unknown keys are dropped silently. The renderer receives the whole config as boot.config: from "init", and again after every save through applyConfirmedPreferences → setBoot({config:saved}). preferences.mjs is also imported by the renderer, so it and everything it imports must stay pure (no node:*).
2. Packaging drops node_modules (`--ignore=…node_modules…`), so app/electron/* may only require node:* and electron. YAML or frontmatter parsing must happen in the renderer: the `yaml` package is already a dependency and is used in src/skill-file-model.mjs. The overlay file can be written as JSON, because JSON is valid YAML.
3. Renderer CSP allows img data:, inline <style> and font data:.
4. Bridge (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/index.js):
   - createThread/openThread pass a `setup(agentCtx)` hook that already runs installModelSelection. That hook is where agent-scoped prompt sections and request waterfalls go: `agentCtx.get('systemPrompt').section({...})` and `agentCtx.on('agent/request', …)`.
   - LlmCallConfig supports maxTokens and temperature, and dsh-llm-deepseek forwards temperature to the wire. There is NO top_p anywhere, so top_p is skipped.
   - installModelSelection's agent/request listener spreads `...resolved`, so extra fields survive.
   - The bridge ignores developerInstructions today.
5. Custom OpenAI-compatible provider: the Harness already supports one with no new Harness code, through the dormant `llm-pi-ai` row in dsh-base. Its config is `providers: {route: {api, baseURL, apiKeyEnv, models}}`, and credentials-local reads the key from the env var named by apiKeyEnv. In this app it is therefore a profile-overlay row plus an env var for the core process. It is implemented in C5 as a STRETCH item that uses C6's overlay API (see C5).
6. Theme tokens (public/assets/v1/c6a992d55-*.css):
   - Accent: `--cds-role-accent-{50,100,250,300,400,450,600,700,800,850,fill,fill-hover,on}` on :where(:root). The semantic tokens `--cds-fill-accent/--cds-text-accent/--cds-bg-accent/--cds-border-accent/--cds-on-accent` live on `.cds-root` and reference the role tokens.
   - Radii: `--cds-radius--xs/--sm/--lg/--cds-radius-composer` on `.cds-root`, with a `[data-density=comfortable]` variant. Tailwind `--radius-xs…3xl` on :root.
   - Type scale: `--cds-rem-scale: calc(16 / 17)` on :root.
   - Fonts: `--cds-font-sans` on .cds-root (dyslexic override in shared-styles); `--font-ui` on :root; `--cds-font-mono:var(--cds-font-mono-override,) …` on :root. main.jsx already sets `--cds-font-code/--cds-font-mono` inline for codeFont.
7. Test constraints that shape the nav:
   - skills-mcp asserts nav groups exactly ["Settings","Desktop app","Customize"] and Customize = ["Skills","Connectors","Plugins"].
   - settings-complete presses End in the narrow tablist and expects "Plugins" to be the last tab.
   - Settings search for 'transcript' must give exactly 1 hit + 3 children; 'mcp' and 'awake' are also asserted.
   - So NO tab is added to the Customize group or after Plugins, and new tab labels/keywords must avoid transcript/mcp/fast/awake.
8. The Settings focus trap selector (source-settings.jsx ~L311) omits textarea. C1 fixes it for everyone.
9. Codex core (fixtures in app/tests/fixtures, CODE_DESKTOP_CORE=codex) must keep working. All bridge-bound extras travel only when `client.serverInfo?.engine === 'deepseek-harness'`, under the namespaced `params.codeDesktop` object, which is the same pattern as the existing permission hints.

Parallel-edit protocol (applies to every agent):
- Prefer new files.
- In shared hot files, use the Edit tool against the exact anchor strings given in each spec. An anchor is a line that stays intact after the other agents insert their lines next to it.
- When Edit reports the file changed, re-read it and retry.
- Never reformat or reorder lines you do not own.
- Build and run your suites only after `npm run build` succeeds. If the build fails on a missing file another agent owns, wait or poll; do not create their file. The two exceptions are the C1 settings kit and the C5 model-params stub, which C1 may create from the exact contents given in the schema.
- Do not kill the user's running Code Desktop. No `npm start`, no visible windows. Use DSH_HOME=<scratchpad>/dsh-home for any live DeepSeek run.
schema:
ONE SHARED PREFERENCES SCHEMA (preferences.json top-level keys; one key per feature, each a whole object; the renderer always sends the WHOLE object for its key by read-modify-write; null resets the key to its default). Each key has its own pure validator module in a NEW folder app/electron/prefs/.mjs (no node:* imports, renderer-safe). Each module exports: - DEFAULT (frozen) - normalize(value): lenient read; always returns a valid object; used by the renderer and main - validate(value): strict; throws Error(''); returns the normalized object, or null when value === null Wiring in app/electron/preferences.mjs (each owner adds exactly 2 lines): - (a) An import line inserted directly after the anchor line `import { DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_VIEW, TRANSCRIPT_VIEWS } from './transcript-view-model.mjs';` - (b) One line inserted directly before the anchor ` return next;\n}` that ends settingsPatch: `if ('' in patch) { const v = validate(patch.); if (v === null) delete next.; else next. = v; }` No other preferences.mjs edits. main.cjs's "settings" case already routes everything through settingsPatch. KEYS 1. customInstructions (C1; file prefs/instructions.mjs; exports validateInstructions/normalizeInstructions/INSTRUCTIONS_DEFAULT) - Shape: { enabled: boolean = true, global: string = '' (≤20000 chars, \r\n→\n, no NUL), projects: { [absFolderPath]: { text: string ≤20000, useFile: boolean = true } } } - Limits: ≤64 project entries; a key must be an absolute POSIX path ≤1024 chars without NUL; entries with empty text and useFile true are dropped. - Project resolution: the longest key equal to cwd or a parent of cwd wins. - Project file: the nearest `/.code-desktop/instructions.md`, walking up from cwd at most 8 levels and stopping at $HOME or /. It is read only when useFile !== false. Cap 32 KB. 2. persona (C2; prefs/persona.mjs) - Shape: { assistantName: string = '' (≤40, no control chars or <>; '' means 'DeepSeek'), greeting: string = '' (≤120; template; '{name}' = user displayName; '' means the built-in "What’s up next…" copy), sparkIcon: 'spark'|'star'|'lightning'|'chat'|'custom' = 'spark', sparkImage: string = '' (must match /^data:image\/(png|jpeg|webp|svg\+xml);base64,[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/, ≤350000 chars; required when sparkIcon is 'custom') } - The user display name stays the EXISTING top-level key `displayName` (unchanged). 3. customCommands (C3; prefs/custom-commands.mjs) - Shape: { globalDir: string = '' ('' means /commands; otherwise an absolute path ≤1024), projectEnabled: boolean = true } - The command files themselves live on disk, not in prefs. 4. customTheme (C4; prefs/theme.mjs) - Shape: { preset: string = 'default' (≤40, informational), accent: string = '' ('' or #rrggbb), uiFont: string = '' (≤120; same charset rule as codeFont: no ;{}<> or control chars), fontScale: number = 1 (0.85–1.25, step 0.05), density: 'compact'|'comfortable' = 'compact', radiusScale: number = 1 (0–2, step 0.25) } - Code font and code themes stay in the EXISTING keys codeFont, codeThemeLight and codeThemeDark (validated as today). The theme JSON file bundles them: theme file = {"format":"code-desktop-theme","version":1,"name":string,"accent","uiFont","fontScale","density","radiusScale","codeFont","codeThemeLight","codeThemeDark"} - Import → one settings patch {customTheme, codeFont, codeThemeLight, codeThemeDark}. Unknown code themes are dropped to the defaults with a warning. 5. modelSettings (C5; prefs/model-settings.mjs) - Shape: { params: { [modelId]: { maxTokens?: int 256..1000000, temperature?: number 0..2 (2 decimals), effort?: string ≤32 /^[a-z0-9_-]+$/ } }, prices: null | { [modelId]: { displayName?: string ≤60, offPeak: {cacheHit, cacheMiss, output}, peak: {cacheHit, cacheMiss, output} } } } - Default: { params:{}, prices:null }. - modelId: string ≤128 /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:\/-]+$/, ≤50 entries per map. Prices are CNY per 1M tokens, finite, 0–10000. - prices null means the official table. 6. harnessProfile (C6; prefs/harness-profile.mjs) - Shape: { overlayEnabled: boolean = true } - The overlay's content is NOT in prefs. It is app-managed state in /harness/overlay.json, rendered to /harness/overlay.patch.yml (JSON text). The power-user hand-edited file is /harness/user.patch.yml. HOW VALUES REACH THE CORE (one transport, no new push RPC, stateless and robust to core restarts) A. main.cjs desktop:call "rpc" case. Decorators run after validateBypassRequest and before client.request; each owns one insertion. - DeepSeek engine (client.serverInfo?.engine === 'deepseek-harness'): methods thread/start, thread/resume and turn/start get `params.codeDesktop = { ...params.codeDesktop, customization: { ...params.codeDesktop?.customization, : value } }` - instructions (C1): string|null. This is the final composed text exactly as shown in the preview, ≤40000 chars. - modelParams (C5): { [wireModelId]: { maxTokens?, temperature? } } | null - account/usage/read gets `params.codeDesktop = { ...params.codeDesktop, prices: }` (C5). - Codex engine: only C1 acts. It appends the composed text to params.developerInstructions on thread/start. On thread/resume it does the same only if the field exists in work/codex-schema-0.155.1 ThreadResumeParams; otherwise not. Nothing else is sent to Codex. - The cwd for composition is params.cwd, falling back to config.threadMetadata[params.threadId]?.cwd, then config.cwd. B. Bridge (harness/packages/codex-app-server/src): - customization.js (C1) exports: - `createCustomRef()` → { instructions: undefined, modelParams: undefined } - `applyCustomization(ref, params)`: reads params?.codeDesktop?.customization. A key that is present (including null) replaces the ref field; normalizeModelParams comes from model-params.js. - `installCustomization(agentCtx, ref, { catalog })`: calls installInstructions(agentCtx, ref) from instructions.js and installModelParams(agentCtx, ref, { catalog }) from model-params.js. - instructions.js (C1) registers the agent-scoped section `{ name: 'code-desktop:custom-instructions', order: systemPrompt.getSectionOrder('DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_SUFFIX') + 50, interpolate: false, text: () => ref.instructions ?? '' }`. The text is evaluated at each assembly, so a change applies from the next step or message. - model-params.js (C5) exports `installModelParams(agentCtx, ref, { catalog })`. It registers `agentCtx.on('agent/request', async (_p, next) => { const cfg = await next(); … })`. The listener strips temperature and the user-added maxTokens when no entry applies, and sets them from ref.modelParams[catalog.wireId(cfg.provider, cfg.model)] when one does. It also exports `normalizeModelParams(value)`. - If C1 needs model-params.js before C5 lands, C1 creates this exact stub: `export function normalizeModelParams(value){return value&&typeof value==='object'?value:undefined} export function installModelParams(){return ()=>{}}` C5 then replaces the whole file. - pricing.js and usage.js (C5): prices are passed down from account/usage/read params.codeDesktop.prices, merged over DEEPSEEK_PRICES, and re-validated in the bridge. - New bridge RPCs. They are called by main-process modules directly via client.request, never added to the renderer rpc allowlist, and a METHOD_NOT_FOUND from Codex means "unavailable": - codeDesktop/pricing/read → { official: DEEPSEEK_PRICES, aliases, pricingUrl, peakWindows: 'Beijing Mon–Fri 09–12, 14–18' } (C5) - codeDesktop/profile/read → see C6 C. Renderer-only features (C2, C3, C4) read boot.config through their normalize() functions. They never send anything to the core except C3, whose expanded command text is ordinary message text. SETTINGS PAGE CONTRACT (C1 creates first; everyone uses it) - New file app/src/source-settings-kit.jsx exports: - `SettingRow({row,error})`: moved verbatim from source-settings.jsx L324-331 (same classes, data-setting-id, below slot) - `SettingsGroup({title,rows=[],rowErrors={},children})`: renders `

{title}

{rows.map(r=>)}{children}
` - `settingRow(id,label,description,control,extra={})` → {id,label,description,control,...extra} - A tab entry may carry `page: Component`. source-settings.jsx renders `{activeTab?.page && }` inside .ss-content, right after `{customizePage}`, where: `pageProps = { config, boot, model, effort, busy, engine, desktopCall, onSave, onReconnect, customize, cwd: customize?.cwd ?? config.cwd, threadId: customize?.threadId ?? null }` - Pages own their optimistic state and errors, and use the row-below error text "Couldn’t save the setting. Try again." with the reason in title, as SettingRow does. - Main-process feature modules follow one pattern: - `create({ app, dialog, shell, getConfig: () => config, getClient: () => client, emit, getWindow: () => win, knownCwd: (cwd) => workspaceQueryRoot(cwd) })` returns `{ run(p), …hooks }`. - The require goes after the main.cjs anchor `const {mcpDefinitions,storageReport,storageCoreRoot,editConfigTarget,recordSettingsFailure} = require("./settings-pages.cjs");` - The instantiation goes after the anchor line beginning `const customizeOperations = createCustomizeOperations(` - The single desktop:call case uses the anchors listed per feature.
settingsIA:
Final Settings navigation. Fidelity tests pin the group titles, the Customize group's members, and Plugins as the last narrow tab, so new pages go into the existing "Settings" and "Desktop app" groups only.

Settings group, in order:
- Preferences
- Theme (C4, NEW, icon 'Palette', keywords ['accent','colors','font size','corner radius','density','appearance'])
- Usage (navHidden, unchanged)
- Code
- Instructions (C1, NEW, icon 'BookText', keywords ['custom instructions','system prompt','agents.md','project instructions'])
- Commands (C3, NEW, icon 'SlashShortcutCommand', keywords ['slash commands','prompt templates','custom commands'])
- Models (C5, NEW, icon 'Lightning', keywords ['max tokens','temperature','pricing','prices','cost'])

Desktop app group:
- General
- Developer
- Harness (C6, NEW, icon 'CommandLine', keywords ['cordis','profile','bundles','hooks','harness plugins','overlay'])

Customize group: Skills, Connectors, Plugins. UNCHANGED, still last.

Tab-line insertion anchors in the `tabs` array of app/src/source-settings.jsx. They are designed to give a deterministic final order whatever order the agents edit in:
- C4: replace `  {id:'preferences',label:'Preferences',icon:'Settings',group:'Settings',keywords:['general']},` with itself + the theme line.
- C1: replace `  {id:'code',label:'Code',icon:'Code',group:'Settings'},` with itself + the instructions line.
- C5: insert the models line DIRECTLY BEFORE `  {id:'general',label:'General',icon:'Computer',group:'Desktop app'},`
- C3: insert the commands line directly before the `  {id:'models',` line if it exists, otherwise directly before the general line.
- C6: replace `  {id:'developer',label:'Developer',icon:'Wrench',group:'Desktop app'},` with itself + the harness line.

Each line has the form `{id:'<id>',label:'<Label>',icon:'<Icon>',group:'<Group>',keywords:[…],page:<Component>}` with ids theme / instructions / commands / models / harness. No `customize:true` flag; the pages use the normal .ss-content layout.

Search indexing: new pages are found by label and keywords only (no group rows). Never use the words transcript, mcp, fast or awake in labels or keywords.

Placement of persona (C2): no new tab. A new "Persona" group goes on the Preferences page directly after "Profile", which keeps the existing "What should we call you?" displayName row. The rows are:
- Assistant name: text field with Save. Placeholder 'DeepSeek'. Description: "Shown in approval titles, notifications and the transcript."
- Home greeting: text field. Placeholder "What’s up next, {name}?" plus help text naming the {name} token.
- Assistant icon: SourceSegments of the glyphs Spark / Star / Lightning / Chat / Custom image, with a "Choose image…" button and a 24px preview.
- Reset persona: SourceSettingsButton variant secondary.

What each new page contains, all built from SourceSelect, SourceSwitch, SourceSegments, SourceSettingsButton, SourceDialog and the existing ss-* classes:
- Theme (C4):
  - Presets row: SourceSelect, plus Import… / Export… / Reset to default buttons.
  - "Colors" group: accent color input[type=color] + hex text + Clear.
  - "Typography" group: UI font combobox (system font list + free text), Code font (reuses SourceCodeFontSetting bound to the existing codeFont key), Font size segments 85–125%, Density segments Compact/Comfortable.
  - "Shape" group: corner radius segments Sharp(0) / Subtle(0.5) / Default(1) / Round(1.5) / Extra(2).
  - "Code theme" group: the same two-column light/dark SourceSelect + SourceCodeThemePreview as the Code page, bound to the existing codeThemeLight/codeThemeDark keys.
  - A live preview card: button, accent chip, link, code block, composer-radius box.
  - The Code page keeps its existing rows unchanged.
- Instructions (C1):
  - "Global instructions" group: enabled switch; a large textarea (min 12 rows, monospace, character count "n / 20,000"); Save/Revert buttons. Uses manual save, like SourceProfileSetting / manual-text-save.mjs.
  - "Project instructions" group: project SourceSelect (current cwd + known folders from config.threadMetadata cwds); "Use .code-desktop/instructions.md" switch with file status (path, exists, size) and "Open file" / "Create file" buttons; project override textarea with count.
  - "Preview" group: read-only pre of the exact final appended text, with character count and truncation note, refreshed on save and on project change.
  - A "When it applies" note. DeepSeek core: "from your next message in any session". Codex: "new sessions and sessions reopened after a restart".
  - A "Reset instructions" button.
- Commands (C3):
  - Two lists: "Project commands" (<cwd>/.code-desktop/commands) and "Your commands" (global dir). Each row shows /name, description, argument hint, a 'shadowed by …' badge when applicable, and Edit / Delete (move to Trash).
  - "New command" opens a SourceDialog editor: name, description, argument hint, body textarea, scope select.
  - Rows for the folder location (Change… / Reveal) and the project commands switch.
- Models (C5):
  - One "Model defaults" group per model in boot.models (title = displayName): Max output tokens (number, placeholder 'Default'), Temperature (number 0–2 step 0.1, placeholder 'Default'), Default reasoning effort (SourceSelect: 'Model default' + supportedReasoningEfforts).
  - A note "top_p is not supported by the DeepSeek Harness adapter."
  - A "Pricing" group: an editable table per priced model with Off-peak/Peak × Cache hit / Cache miss / Output, CNY per 1M; "Add model price"; "Reset to official prices"; the official pricing link via desktopCall('external').
  - With a Codex core: one notice "Model parameters and pricing apply with the DeepSeek core." and the controls disabled.
- Harness (C6):
  - "Profile" group: Open profile folder, Edit profile patch (user.patch.yml), Open app overlay, Use app overlay switch, Restart core (onReconnect), Reset overlay.
  - "Plugins and bundles" group: bundle rows with per-row SourceSwitch for safe rows only; core rows show 'Required'.
  - "MCP servers" group: list, Add server (stdio/http dialog), Remove (overlay-added rows only) or Disable.
  - "Skill folders" group: customSkillDirs list with Add folder… / Remove.
  - "Hooks" group: hook rows with enable/disable.
  - A pending-changes banner "Restart the core to apply" with a Restart button.
  - With a Codex core or a missing RPC: one notice and no controls.

features.spec:
CUSTOM SYSTEM PROMPT: global and per-project instructions, injected by the bridge.

Prefs: key customInstructions (see schema). New file app/electron/prefs/instructions.mjs (validateInstructions, normalizeInstructions, INSTRUCTIONS_DEFAULT).

Main process, new file app/electron/instructions-service.cjs:
- Pure helpers (exported for tests):
  - findProjectFile(cwd, {home, fs}): walks up ≤8 levels to the nearest .code-desktop/instructions.md; stops at home or /.
  - composeInstructions({prefs, cwd, fileText, filePath}) → {text, parts:[{source:'global'|'projectFile'|'projectOverride', path?, chars}], chars, truncated}. Format:
    `# Custom instructions\n<global>`
    `\n\n# Project instructions (<root>)\n<file text>\n\n<override text>`
    Empty parts are omitted. Total capped at 40000 chars with a trailing '[truncated]' line. enabled:false → empty text.
  - decorateCoreParams(method, params, {engine, prefs, cwd, read}).
- createInstructionsService({getConfig, getClient, shell, knownCwd}) → {run(p), decorate(method, params)}.
- run ops:
  - 'preview' {cwd} → composition + {file:{path, exists, bytes}}
  - 'create-file' {cwd}: mkdir -p and write a short commented template only if the file is absent, then shell.openPath
  - 'open-file' {cwd}
  - 'reveal-file' {cwd}
  Every op validates cwd through knownCwd.
- decorate():
  - DeepSeek (getClient().serverInfo?.engine==='deepseek-harness') and method ∈ {thread/start, thread/resume, turn/start}: sets params.codeDesktop.customization.instructions = text || null, merging and never clobbering other keys.
  - Codex and method === 'thread/start' with non-empty text: params.developerInstructions = [existing, text].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n'). Do the same for thread/resume ONLY if work/codex-schema-0.155.1 ThreadResumeParams has developerInstructions.
  - The file is read fresh on every call (no cache needed; 32 KB cap).

Bridge:
- New harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/instructions.js: installInstructions(agentCtx, ref). Registers the scoped section via agentCtx.get('systemPrompt'); a no-op if the service is absent. Returns the disposer.
- New customization.js: createCustomRef, applyCustomization, installCustomization (see schema). Imports installModelParams/normalizeModelParams from model-params.js; create the exact stub from the schema if C5 has not created it yet.
- Do NOT start honoring developerInstructions (the renderer's hardcoded 'Do not claim to be Claude' string must keep being ignored on DeepSeek).
- Subagent children do not inherit the instructions; document this.

Renderer:
- First create app/src/source-settings-kit.jsx (schema contract) and move SettingRow there; source-settings.jsx imports it.
- New app/src/source-settings-instructions.jsx exporting SourceInstructionsSettings(pageProps); layout per settingsIA.
  - Saving sends the WHOLE customInstructions object via onSave.
  - Textareas use manual save (Save/Revert); count shown as `${n.toLocaleString()} / 20,000`.
  - The preview calls desktopCall('instructions',{op:'preview',cwd}).
  - The project list comes from cwd plus unique config.threadMetadata[*].cwd (≤20).
  - Engine note from pageProps.engine (coreEngine).
- New app/src/instructions-settings.css for any extra styles (ss-* tokens only, light and dark via CDS vars).

Owned generic Settings mechanism in source-settings.jsx (only C1 touches these):
- pageProps const + page render
- focus-trap selector gains textarea
- SettingRow moved to the kit

Docs: README subsection (anchor below).

Live check (optional): DSH_HOME=<scratch>/dsh-home with global text 'End every reply with the word PINEAPPLE.' → a new session's reply ends with PINEAPPLE; change the text → the next message in the same session follows it.

It (re)arms fs.watch on both dirs (and the parent .code-desktop when the commands dir is missing). Debounce 150 ms, then emit({kind:'custom-commands-changed', scope, cwd}). Keep ≤8 project watchers (LRU) and close all on app quit. - 'save' {scope:'global'|'project', cwd?, name, previousName?, text}: validate the name and size, mkdir -p, atomic write (tmp + rename), rename when previousName differs. If neither is present and args is non-empty, append '\n\n'+args. - mergeCommands({global, project, builtinIds, skillNames}) → [{name, description, argumentHint, body, scope, path, shadowedBy?}]. Prefs: key customTheme (schema) plus the EXISTING codeFont / codeThemeLight / codeThemeDark. New app/electron/prefs/theme.mjs.

New app/src/theme-custom-model.mjs (pure). Exports:
- THEME_PRESETS: default; deepseek (#4D6BFE); clay (#d97757); forest (#2f855a); grape (#7c3aed); sharp (radius 0); rounded (radius 1.5). Each is a full customTheme object.
- themeRootStyle(theme) → {[prop]: value} for document.documentElement inline style:
  - `--cds-rem-scale: calc(16 / 17 * <fontScale>)`, only when ≠1
  - accent scale on `--cds-role-accent-{50,100,250,300,400,450,600,700,800,850}` derived with CSS `color-mix(in oklab, <accent> p%, white|black)` (450 = accent itself)
  - `--cds-role-accent-fill` = accent; `-fill-hover` = mix 85% with white
  - `--cds-role-accent-on` = '#fff' or '#000' by WCAG relative luminance computed in JS
- themeCss(theme) → text for <style id="code-desktop-custom-theme">. Rules are scoped under `:root[data-custom-theme]` and must outrank `.cds-root`, `.cds-root[data-density=comfortable]` and shared-styles' dyslexic rule:
  - `--font-ui` and `--cds-font-sans: "<uiFont>", var(--cds-font-system)`
  - the radius tokens `--cds-radius--xs/--sm/--lg/--cds-radius-composer` and Tailwind `--radius-*`, scaled by radiusScale. Read the exact compact and comfortable base rem values from public/assets/v1/c6a992d55-*.css and hardcode them with a comment citing them.
- applyCustomTheme(doc, config):
  - sets or removes data-custom-theme and the style element
  - clears every property it set before, so the default theme leaves NO inline props and NO attribute (byte-identical computed styles)
- exportThemeFile(config) / importThemeFile(json) → {patch, warnings}. Validates via prefs/theme.mjs and the code-theme catalog's isTheme.
- themeDensity(config) → 'compact'|'comfortable'
